text:
Alex: heads-up — saw a new class of fragmentation in recent staging runs. after offload we have a bunch of tiny 'ghost' host pages that never get reused and slowly bloat the slab pools :confused:
Maria: can you paste a quick heapdump or allocation sample? curious if it's cross-tenant or pinned to a pool
Alex: pasted below (trimmed). pattern: many 4K/8K fragments marked resident but unmapped in active kvcache. allocator shows holes between live allocations.
```
# slab-summary
pool gpu-staging: total 24G, used 16.2G, free-fragments: 328 (avg 7.2K)
pool host-staging: total 48G, used 33.7G, free-fragments: 1203 (avg 3.9K)
resident-pages: 1.2M, ghost-marked: 84.2K
```
Sam: hmm. sounds like we leave backing pages as 'ghost' after offload to avoid races with in-flight kernels. sticky safety windows?
Taylor: right — earlier offload safety added a grace window for pending reads. we probably never compact those ghosts aggressively because of correctness concerns. long-term that creates fanout fragmentation.
Maria: tradeoffs: eagerly reclaim means risk of recovering pages still referenced by in-flight ops, which could cause wrong data reads. lazy reclaim keeps safety but fragments memory.
Alex: proposal: introduce a "staged-ghost" state with lightweight refcounting + async confirmation. flow: on offload, mark pages as staged-ghost and start a small TTL/confirmation probe. if no confirmation from kernel/hw within X ms, promote to reclaimable; if confirmation arrives, clear staged flag.
Sam: would need a cheap probe — we can't block the whole allocator. maybe piggyback on existing completion queue events rather than new syscalls.
Maria: also need to track contiguous region coalescing. if we only reclaim single pages we'll still leave holes. suggest accumulating contiguous staged-ghost runs and then perform a batched compaction pass when a threshold is met.
Taylor: compaction pass should be prioritized by fragmentation score and tenant QoS. don't run compaction during peak inference windows.
Alex: agreed. rough API surface: allocator.mark_staged(addr, len, ticket_id) and offload-coordinator.confirm(ticket_id) or offload-coordinator.expire(ticket_id). we can reuse current ticketing in offload agent.
Sam: latency concern: compaction + memmove on host staging could bump tail latency for some microbatches. we should prefer moving long-lived cold pages to a compact pool asynchronously.
Maria: instrumentation: add counters for staged-ghost count, avg residency time, coalesced-run-length, compaction cycles, and per-tenant fragmentation delta. perfbot can chart over a week.
perfbot: noted — will add charts for staged_ghost_count, staged_ghost_ttl_miss_rate, staged_coalesce_runs to the eng-runtime dashboard. :white_check_mark:
Alex: quick experiment plan: enable staged-ghost state with TTL=500ms on a canary pool, run mixed workload (small prompt bursty + long prompt) and capture tail p99 tokens/sec and fragmentation delta after 12h.
Taylor: add rollback toggle: immediate-disable compaction and force-mark-all-clear to revert behavior quickly if we see correctness issues.
Sam: question: how do we prove safety? need a small formalization: guarantee that any kernel that could reference a staged page must post a ticket to the offload-coordinator before the page can be reclaimed. that's our contract.
Maria: document that contract in the offload RFC follow-up and attach sequence diagram. I'll draft the diagram and a checklist for perf/QA.
Alex: will open a short RFC PR titled "staged ghost reclamation and coalesced compaction" with measurements and a canary rollout plan. assigning to @Maria for instrumentation and @Sam for microbench harness.
Sam: +1. I'll add a microbench that repeats allocation/offload cycles with varying in-flight depth.
Taylor: also think about backpressure: when fragmentation > threshold, throttle new offloads to force more reuse until compaction completes. otherwise we risk OOM storms.
Alex: good call. add a circuit-breaker config: offload_throttle_pct and frag_threshold_bytes.
Maria: I'll extend telem to expose frag_threshold crossings and throttle events.
perfbot: I added a weekly alert that triggers if staged_ghost_count > 50k for > 10m.
Alex: thanks. let's sync tomorrow 10am to review the RFC draft and canary metrics. :calendar:
Maria: 👍
Sam: 👍
